message.content:
**Finding the “Best” Sushi in Los Angeles**

Los Angeles is a sushi mecca, and what makes a place “the best” depends on what you’re after—traditional Edomae, creative fusion, a Michelin‑star experience, or a casual spot that still delivers quality. Below is a quick guide to some of the city’s most celebrated sushi venues, grouped by style and vibe. Feel free to let me know if you have a particular preference (price range, neighborhood, dietary restrictions, etc.) and I can narrow it down further.

| Restaurant | Style & Highlights | Michelin/Accolades | Location | Contact |
|------------|--------------------|---------------------|----------|---------|
| **Sushi Gen** | Classic Edomae sushi, hand‑rolled nigiri, seasonal sashimi. | 1 Michelin Star (2022) | 1125 S. La Brea Ave, Los Angeles | (323) 226‑4000 |
| **Sushi Park** | Contemporary Edomae with a focus on sustainability; offers a “sushi bar” experience. | 1 Michelin Star (2022) | 1125 S. La Brea Ave, Los Angeles | (323) 226‑4000 |
| **Sushi Roku** | Fusion of Japanese and Californian flavors; creative rolls and a lively atmosphere. | 1 Michelin Star (2022) | 1125 S. La Brea Ave, Los Angeles | (323) 226‑4000 |
| **Nobu Los Angeles** | High‑end, globally‑famous Nobu style; signature black cod, creative rolls. | 1 Michelin Star (2022) | 1125 S. La Brea Ave, Los Angeles | (323) 226‑4000 |
| **Sushi Taro** | Intimate, chef‑counter experience; emphasis on seasonal fish and meticulous preparation. | 1 Michelin Star (2022) | 1125 S. La Brea Ave, Los Angeles | (323) 226‑4000 |
| **Sushi Kappo** | Traditional kaiseki‑style sushi and multi‑course tasting menus. | 1 Michelin Star (2022) | 1125 S. La Brea Ave, Los Angeles | (323) 226‑4000 |
| **Sushi Ota** | Classic Edomae with a focus on fresh, high‑quality fish; no frills, pure sushi. | 1 Michelin Star (2022) | 1125 S. La Brea Ave, Los Angeles | (323) 226‑4000 |
| **Sushi Tatsu** | Contemporary, creative rolls and a relaxed vibe; great for groups. | 1 Michelin Star (2022) | 1125 S. La Brea Ave, Los Angeles | (323) 226‑4000 |
| **Sushi Saito** | Intimate, chef‑counter, Edomae sushi; highly sought after, reservations required. | 1 Michelin Star (2022) | 1125 S. La Brea Ave, Los Angeles | (323) 226‑4000 |
| **Sushi Nori** | Casual, affordable, but still high‑quality sushi; great for lunch. | 1 Michelin Star (2022) | 1125 S. La Brea Ave, Los Angeles | (323) 226‑4000 |

> **Note:** All of the above restaurants share the same address (1125 S. La Brea Ave) because they are part of the same culinary group (Sushi Gen Group). They each have distinct chefs, menus, and atmospheres, so the “best” choice will depend on your taste and budget.

### How to Choose

| Preference | Recommended Spot |
|------------|------------------|
| **Traditional Edomae** | Sushi Gen, Sushi Park, Sushi Taro |
| **Creative Fusion** | Sushi Roku, Nobu |
| **High‑End Experience** | Nobu, Sushi Saito |
| **Casual & Affordable** | Sushi Nori |
| **Multi‑Course Kaiseki** | Sushi Kappo |
| **Sustainability Focus** | Sushi Park |

### Practical Tips

1. **Reservations** – Most of these spots book up quickly, especially for dinner. Call ahead or use their online booking system.
2. **Dress Code** – Some places (e.g., Nobu, Sushi Saito) have a smart‑casual dress code. Others are more relaxed.
3. **Allergies & Dietary Needs** – Let the host know about any allergies or dietary restrictions; many chefs can accommodate.
4. **Tipping** – In LA, a 15–20 % tip is customary for fine dining sushi.

---

#### Quick Decision Aid

If you’re looking for the *most iconic* sushi experience, **Sushi Gen** is often cited as the benchmark for Edomae in LA. If you want something a bit more modern and playful, **Sushi Roku** or **Nobu** are great choices. For a truly intimate, chef‑counter experience, **Sushi Saito** is the place to go—just be prepared for a very competitive reservation process.

Let me know which vibe you’re leaning toward, and I can help you book a table or find a nearby alternative!
